children: VANCOUVER, Canada, Nov. 20, 2026
Sonoro Gold Corp.

(TSXV: SGO | OTCQB: SMOFF | FRA: 23SP) (“Sonoro” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce the completion of a comprehensive geotechnical investigation program and the commencement of advanced engineering for a proposed open pit, mining operation at its Cerro Caliche gold project in Sonora, Mexico.

The Company engaged BBA Consultants International LP (“BBA”) to oversee geotechnical investigations and develop the feasibility-level engineering design for the proposed heap leach facility as part of the overall feasibility study, with Ausenco Mexico S. de R.L. de C.V. (“Ausenco”) serving as the lead engineering consultant for the overall project. The extensive geotechnical and geophysical investigations have now been completed with advanced engineering and the HLF design expected to be finalized by the end of Q1 in 2027.
The programs mark important advancements of Cerro Caliche and are expected to provide key technical inputs for project design, development planning, and ongoing permitting activities.
“The geotechnical investigations and advanced engineering are fundamental to both the design criteria and structural integrity of the proposed Cerro Caliche operation,”
said Kenneth MacLeod, President and CEO.

“This work reflects additional de-risking milestones at Cerro Caliche while we continue with our very successful drilling program which has identified higher-grade mineralization at the recently acquired Diana and Batamote concessions.”
Geotechnical Investigation Programs

BBA coordinated and provided technical oversight of the geotechnical and geophysical investigation programs conducted by specialized third-party contractors to support the feasibility-level engineering design of the proposed heap leach facility. The investigations covered the proposed heap leach pad, solution ponds, crushing plant, ancillary facilities, waste rock area, and other areas across the project site. Field activities included geophysical surveys, borehole drilling, test pit excavations, and piezometer installations.
Eight HQ-size geotechnical boreholes were completed to characterize subsurface soil and bedrock conditions. In addition, 16 test pits were excavated to depths ranging from 1.40 to 5.80 meters.

Onsite Standard Penetration Tests (SPT) were carried out in the soil intervals and permeability testing to evaluate the hydraulic conditions and laboratory testing was conducted on soil and rock samples taken from the boreholes and pits to adequately characterize foundation soils.

The results and details from the site work are being used for the final heap leach design to a feasibility level with full details of water balance, material take-offs of the liner system and water diversion requirements.
The geotechnical results are expected to be instrumental for project development and are currently being utilized as key inputs into the advanced engineering phase currently underway.
Advanced Engineering
Advanced engineering is being led by Ausenco Mexico, a global engineering, consultancy and project delivery company specializing in the mining and metals industry.

The scope of work is to further define key components of the proposed mining operation, incorporating the results of recent geotechnical work, as well as environmental and engineering studies completed across the project site.

The engineering work is expected to provide additional detail regarding site infrastructure, operational design criteria, construction requirements, and implementation planning for the development, construction and commissioning of the process facilities.
